For all SLO ACT clients, functioning in major life domains presents significant personal difficulties. Addressing the rehabilitation needs of clients in these key domains will be the team’s essential purpose. SLO ACT provides a full range of services, including assessment, individualized treatment planning, personal service coordination, integrated co\-occurring mental health and substance use disorder treatment, medication services, and access to support services on a 24/7, 365\-day basis. **Department:** Senior Housing Services (SHS)


**Status:**Full\-time non\-exempt


**Hours**: Monday\-Friday, 8:30 AM –5:00 PM


**Compensation:**$30\.00 per hour


**Reports to:** Senior Housing Services Manager

 **About Us**



St. Mary's Center is a community of hope, healing, and justice dedicated to helping older adults age with dignity by addressing housing instability, poverty, food insecurity, and social isolation. Through our Aging with Dignity model, we provide a continuum of person\-centered services, including street outreach, coordinated entry, housing navigation, transitional housing, tenancy sustaining services, aging in place supports, and a vibrant Community Center, while empowering older adults to shape solutions through leadership and advocacy.

  

This is an exciting time to join St. Mary's Center. We are growing our impact, strengthening our programs, modernizing our systems, and expanding affordable housing opportunities for older adults in partnership with community organizations. We are seeking passionate, collaborative professionals who are energized by innovation, committed to excellence, and inspired to make a meaningful difference in the lives of older adults every day.

 **Position Summary**



The Housing Navigator assists older adults experiencing homelessness or housing instability in obtaining permanent housing. The position is responsible for housing search, document readiness, landlord engagement, housing applications, and move\-in coordination.



Participants must complete Coordinated Entry and assessment requirements prior to enrollment in Housing Navigation services when applicable.



Minimum caseload is 30 active participants.

 **Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

  

Housing Search \& Placement (40%)


* Conduct housing\-focused navigation.
* Assist participants with housing search activities.
* Identify affordable and supportive housing opportunities.
* Complete and submit housing applications.
* Track housing opportunities and participant progress.
* Coordinate housing interviews and lease\-up.

  



Housing Passport \& Document Readiness (20%)


* Assist participants with obtaining identification and required documents.
* Maintain Housing Passport documentation.
* Coordinate income verification and benefit documentation.
* Ensure housing application packets are complete.

  



Landlord \& Housing Provider Engagement (15%)


* Develop and maintain landlord relationships.
* Coordinate with housing providers and property managers.
* Advocate on behalf of participants.
* Support housing placement negotiations.

  



Move\-In Coordination (15%)


* Coordinate participant move\-ins.
* Assist with housing transition activities.
* Coordinate with Housing Pathways and TSS Program Coordinator for service handoffs.
* Support participant housing orientation activities.

  



Documentation \& Compliance (10%)


* Maintain HMIS and Salesforce documentation.
* Complete Housing Support Plans.
* Document participant services timely and accurately.
* Participate in case conferences and quality assurance reviews.

  


**Performance Expectations**


* Minimum caseload of 30 participants maintained.
* Housing placement goals achieved.
* Housing applications submitted timely.
* Documentation standards met.
* Housing Passport completion targets achieved.
* Successful transition of housed participants to TSS services.

  


**Qualifications**


* We welcome candidates with an Associate degree in psychology, sociology, behavioral science, or a related field, or two or more years of experience in housing, homelessness, social services, or community\-based programs.
* One or more years of experience supporting older adults with co\-occurring mental health, substance use, or other complex needs, including intensive case management, is preferred.
* Must be able to work collaboratively within a strong team environment, and manage designated tasks independently.
* Current, valid CDL.

  


**General Staff Expectations**


* Promote a safe, respectful, and inclusive environment.
* Support the mission and values of St. Mary’s Center.
* Maintain professionalism and confidentiality.
* Follow agency policies and procedures.

  


**Physical Requirements**



The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. In general, while performing the duties of this job, the employee is expected to stand; walk; sit; reach with hands and arms; and talk or hear.


* Ability to sit, stand, walk, bend, and communicate effectively throughout the workday.
* Ability to travel to participant encampments or community sites.
* Ability to occasionally lift and/or move up to 20 pounds.
* Ability to use computers, phones, tablets, and related technology for documentation and communication.

  


**Equal Employment Opportunity**



St. Mary’s Center is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to an active Equal Employment Opportunity. We celebrate diversity and are committed to an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information or veteran status.



In compliance with the California Fair Chance Act, St. Mary’s Center will consider qualified applicant with a criminal history pursuant to the California Fair Chance Act.

About RISE Academy



RISE Academy is a subsidiary of RISE Education System, a 501(c)(3\) nonprofit educational organization accredited by the Western Association of Schools and Colleges (WASC) and Cognia. Our mission is to promote the holistic development of the child through an authentic and experiential student learning experience. This is accomplished by educating the child in the formation of faith, family, and community.



RISE Academy strives to develop the whole child by providing excellence in academic preparation within a faith\-based environment. Our vision is to guide and nurture students to become role models who exhibit high levels of God\-consciousness, professional excellence, and civic leadership through service to society at large.

  

Position Overview



RISE Academy is seeking a part\-time, in\-person After\-School Program Coordinator to support and lead our after\-school program at our campus in San Jose, California.



The After\-School Program Coordinator will report to the Head of Development and will provide leadership, supervision, and support for a holistic, multi\-age after\-school program serving students Monday through Thursday from 2:45 PM to 5:15 PM.



The Coordinator will help create a safe, structured, engaging, and nurturing environment that educates, enriches, and inspires students beyond the regular school day.

  

Job Expectations



Shared Vision



Supports RISE Academy’s vision of excellence for all students and approaches the work with a sense of care, responsibility, and urgency to help students thrive.



Culture of Excellence



Helps foster a safe, respectful, culturally responsive, and nurturing environment where students feel welcomed, supported, and excited to participate.



Professional Growth



Demonstrates a commitment to continuous growth, participates in required trainings, and contributes positively to the school’s professional community.



Community Engagement



Communicates regularly and professionally with families, staff, and school leaders, and supports key school community events when needed.

  

Responsibilities



The After\-School Program Coordinator’s responsibilities include, but are not limited to:


* Plan and implement the daily after\-school program in alignment with the school’s mission, values, and expectations.
* Create a structured, engaging, and developmentally appropriate environment for students across multiple age groups.
* Lead academic, cultural, recreational, and enrichment activities, including preparing necessary supplies and materials.
* Supervise students in classrooms, activity areas, outdoor spaces, and other designated program locations.
* Use age\-appropriate methods rooted in positive youth development principles.
* Maintain a safe environment and respond appropriately to student needs, conflicts, injuries, or emergencies.
* Communicate with school staff, parents, and administrators regarding program activities, student needs, behavior, academic support, and events.
* Maintain a professional attitude, appearance, and rapport with students, families, staff, and community members.
* Support the promotion of the after\-school program, including assisting with basic marketing materials and family communication.
* Attend required staff meetings, trainings, and professional development sessions.
* Support off\-site after\-school field trips, when applicable.
* Assist with administrative tasks related to the after\-school program and other duties as assigned, with the possibility of additional hours depending on program needs.

  

  

Required Skills and Qualifications


* Experience working with students in a recreational, educational, school, or community youth setting.
* Ability to work effectively and collaboratively with students, staff, parents, and community members.
* Strong communication, organization, and supervision skills.
* Familiarity with quality practices for after\-school or youth development programs.
* Ability to demonstrate patience, professionalism, sound judgment, and sensitivity to the needs of students and families.
* Ability to respond calmly and swiftly in critical incidents or emergency situations.
* CPR and First Aid certification, or willingness to obtain certification.
* Physical ability to stand, walk, bend, kneel, and actively supervise students for extended periods of time.
* Physical ability to lead, supervise, and participate in structured indoor and outdoor student activities.
* Ability to lift and carry up to 25 pounds, including program supplies, activity materials, and other items as needed.

  

  

Preferred Qualifications


* Two or more years of experience working with children in an educational or youth development environment.
* Experience planning or coordinating student activities, enrichment programming, or after\-school programming.

Compensation is based on experience, education, certifications, and the scope of assigned responsibilities. Children of eligible staff members may qualify for tuition discounts in accordance with RISE Academy’s staff discount policy.
